---
title: "Example Notebooks"
description: "Short R notebooks: build a diabetes cohort, clean the data, and run Table One, regression, and survival analyses"
---

These R notebooks walk through a complete study comparing people **with** and **without diabetes**, including time to chronic kidney disease (CKD). **Each notebook does one thing**, so each can be taught as its own short class.

|---|---|---|---|

| `0.0 setup` | Checks your settings and the connection to the data | Any | [View](https://github.com/CWML/All-of-Us-Training-Resources/blob/main/notebooks/0.0%20setup.ipynb) · [Download](https://github.com/CWML/All-of-Us-Training-Resources/raw/main/notebooks/0.0%20setup.ipynb) |

Also shows how to use a Data Explorer export instead. | 1 | [View](https://github.com/CWML/All-of-Us-Training-Resources/blob/main/notebooks/1.1%20build_cohorts.ipynb) · [Download](https://github.com/CWML/All-of-Us-Training-Resources/raw/main/notebooks/1.1%20build_cohorts.ipynb) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[22,50,8,20]"}

**Variables used:** age, gender, race, ethnicity; two PTSD survey questions (seeing a doctor, receiving treatment); BMI, systolic blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, and HbA1c; diabetes and CKD diagnoses; visit dates.

## How they fit together

```
aou_setup.R        settings + helpers, loaded by every notebook
     │
1.1 build_cohorts ──► person.csv, survey.csv, measurement.csv
1.2 survival_data ──► survival_conditions.csv, last_visits.csv
     │
2.0 clean_and_join ─► final_analysis.csv, measurements_wide.csv
     │
3.1 table_one · 3.2 logistic · 3.3 linear · 3.4 survival
```

The queries in **1.1** and **1.2** run once and save their results to your bucket. Every later notebook reads those files, so a class can start at any notebook once the data is saved.

## Getting the notebooks into your workspace

The notebooks only run **inside an *All of Us* workspace** (Workbench 2.0): they query the *All of Us* data with BigQuery and save files in your bucket. You'll need the Controlled Tier data collection and a bucket (see [Overview and Resources Tabs](../workspace/resources.qmd#new-cloud-storage-bucket)).

- **Clone this repository:** in your workspace, go to **Apps** → **Git repositories** → **+ Add repository** and enter `https://github.com/CWML/All-of-Us-Training-Resources.git`. It's cloned into apps you create afterward. See the [GitHub Guide](../extras/github-guide.qmd).
- **Download and upload:** download the files above, **including `aou_setup.R`**, and upload them to one folder in your app.

Then launch an R app (e.g., AoU Jupyter with an R kernel; see [Apps](../workspace/apps.qmd)) and **start with `0.0 setup`**: it has you edit two lines in `aou_setup.R`.

**R packages:** `tidyverse`, `lubridate`, `bigrquery`, `broom`, `survival`, `survminer`

::: {.callout-important title="Code only"}
This repository contains **code only, no *All of Us* data**. Clear notebook outputs before sharing or committing, and never publish participant counts of 1 to 20. Notebook 3.1 includes a check for small counts.
:::

The earlier versions of these notebooks (classic Workbench) are kept in [`notebooks/archive`](https://github.com/CWML/All-of-Us-Training-Resources/tree/main/notebooks/archive) for reference.
